given: Circular air capacitor C = 5.00 pF must withstand 100 V while E ≤ 1.00 × 10⁴ N/C.
find: Find minimum gap, minimum plate radius, and maximum charge at 100 V.

title: 24.12 · Cylindrical capacitor
given: Coaxial air capacitor: inner radius a = 2.20 mm, outer inner radius b = 3.50 mm, length L = 2.80 m. Inner conductor is 0.350 V higher.
find: Find capacitance per length and charge on each conductor.
check: The inner conductor is positive and the outer negative; use the inner surface radius of the outer cylinder.

title: 24.14 · Series and parallel capacitors
given: Network A—10 µF—(5 µF in parallel with 8 µF)—9 µF—B; Vₐᵦ = 50.0 V.
find: Find equivalent capacitance, total stored plate charge, and charges on the 10 and 9 µF capacitors.
answer: Ceq = 3.47 µF; total, Q₁₀ and Q₉ = 174 µC each.
check: The 5 and 8 µF branch charges add to the series charge; they are not individually equal to it.

title: 24.24 · Work pulling plates apart
given: Isolated capacitor C = 920 pF carries Q = 3.90 µC. Double the gap, keeping Q constant.
find: Find original and final voltages and external work.
check: Positive work separates attracting plates; the energy doubles.

title: 24.36 · Build a paper capacitor
given: Target C = 1.00 nF. Paper κ = 3.0, sheet thickness 0.20 mm, plate dimensions 22 cm × 28 cm. Posterboard has thickness 12 mm and the same κ.
find: Find the number of paper sheets, the required posterboard plate area, and whether replacing that posterboard with Teflon of the same thickness requires larger or smaller plates.
answer: About 8 sheets; posterboard area 0.452 m²; Teflon needs more area.
note: Use about eight sheets. Teflon has a smaller dielectric constant than the posterboard, so it needs a larger plate area.
check: An integer number of sheets gives an approximate target. For the same thickness and capacitance, lower κ requires larger area.

title: 24.66 · Half-filled dielectric capacitor
given: Square plates 0.120 m on a side, gap d = 4.50 mm; half the area contains Plexiglas κ = 3.40 and half air. Battery stays connected at 18.0 V.
find: Find C, stored energy, and energy after removing the dielectric.

steps.title: Remove the plastic with the battery connected

answer: 62.3 pF; 10.1 nJ initially; 4.59 nJ after removal.
check: The battery fixes voltage, not charge. Using a series-dielectric formula would describe a different geometry.

title: 24.68 · Capacitive fuel gauge
given: Vertical plates have width w, height L and gap d. Fuel fills height h; air above it. κ = 1.95 for gasoline or 33.0 for methanol.
find: Derive effective dielectric constant; evaluate quarter, half and three-quarter full; compare sensitivity.
check: Both are linear in fill height in this ideal model. Methanol gives a larger capacitance change per unit height, making the change easier to resolve.
